LESSON: EXTENSIVE READING: LIBRARY SKILLS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Reading 2.7 Reading Aloud: Dialogue (2 sessions) • Characters • Reading speed an
Topic 2.9: Extensive Reading: Library Skills
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Extensive Reading: Library Skills, part of Reading 2.7 Reading Aloud: Dialogue (2 sessions) • Characters • Reading speed an in Grade 9 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: How can we ensure we pick interesting reading materials easily and fast?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify resources from a collection of materials for reading,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Extensive Reading: Library Skills in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. track reading progress for lifelong learning,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Extensive Reading: Library Skills in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. develop a positive attitude towards reading.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Extensive Reading: Library Skills in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify resources from a collection of materials for reading,

   Extensive Reading: Library Skills helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. track reading progress for lifelong learning,

   Extensive Reading: Library Skills helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. develop a positive attitude towards reading.

   Extensive Reading: Library Skills helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly to discuss factors to consider

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to discuss factors to consider

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Extensive Reading: Library Skills together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and Problem-solving: This is enhanced as the learner explores views when discussing factors to consider when

identifying resources from a wider collection of materials.

Self-efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner effectively orders and prioritises tasks when preparing a reading log to track their

reading progress.

Values:
Love: This is enhanced as the learner displays positive regard for others when conducting a silent reading session with peers to

read grade-appropriate Arabic materials.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental Awareness: This is enhanced as the learners appreciate direction and location to be more aware of their

immediate surroundings.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of keeping reading logs to their learning of similar concepts in English.
